newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi says EU forecasts confirm EMU place.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi says EU forecasts confirm EMU place.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Wednesday European Union forecasts on the Italian economy confirmed that Italy would be in shape to join a single currency from the start.
"This confirms that the government's programme...is valid and realisable," he told a news conference after the EU published forecasts for 1997-98 for the economies of its 15 member states.
The European Commission, in a twice-yearly review of economic conditions, forecast that Italy's Gross Domestic Product would grow by 0.8 percent in 1996 and 1.4 percent in 1997.
It forecast the ratio of public sector deficit to GDP, a key measure under the Maastricht treaty criteria for entry to a single currency, at 6.6 percent this year and 3.3 next year.
Maastricht requires the ratio to be three percent and the EU said 12 countries were so far set to meet the criterion.
Italy's debt to GDP ratio was forecast at 123.4 percent this year and 122.3 percent in 1997 and the GDP price deflator at 3.9 percent this year and 2.9 percent next year.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi has presented a stringent 1997 budget aimed at slashing 62.5 trillion lire off next year's deficit and has repeatedly said it will be tough enough to ensure Italy can join Economic and Monetary Union at the start.
European Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said earlier in Brussels that "the earlier the lira can be brought in (to EMU), the better".
European states hoping to join the single currency, planned for launch in 1999, will be judged early in 1998 on their economic performance in 1997.
